alt: A list of three numbers is converted to three strings, then joined with a space between each pair, giving three characters of data and two separators. The same pattern with a comma gives a comma-separated line. A loop that prints a space after every value would leave one trailing space, shown as an invalid cell.

steps.caption: `nums` holds three numbers. To print them on one line you need text, and `.join()` only accepts text.
`map(str, nums)` converts each number to its text form. Same digits, but each is now a string.
`" ".join(...)` puts one space (shown as a dot) between each pair. Three values have two gaps, and nothing is added before the first or after the last.
`print` shows 3 5 2 and moves to the next line, with no space left at the end.
Changing the separator to `","` changes only the separator: `print` shows 3,5,2. The pattern is the same.
Compare a loop that calls `print(n, end=" ")` for each number. It writes a space after every value, including the last, so the line ends in a trailing space that a judge may reject.
